entities.name: Jakub Kryštof Rad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Jakob Christof Rad was a Swiss-born Austrian physician and industrial manager. He had many other professional activities, was a director of a sugar factory in Dačice, Moravia, Austria-Hungary in 1843, and invented the process and associated machinery for cutting large block sugar into manageable uniform pieces. Rad is credited with the invention of sugar cubes.

He had many other professional activities, was a director of a sugar factory in Dačice, Moravia, Austria-Hungary in 1843, and invented the process and associated machinery for cutting large block sugar into manageable uniform pieces. Rad is credited with the invention of sugar cubes.
